name: Cotton T-shirt
unit: one cotton T-shirt, from field to bin
headline: It took about 2,700 litres of water to make this shirt: what one person drinks in two and a half years.
why: About 7 kg CO₂e to make, plus every wash and tumble-dry.
Cotton is one of the thirstiest crops, often grown in dry regions. Dyeing pollutes rivers.
Safe to wear. Cotton farmers and dye workers face pesticide and chemical exposure.
Cotton uses about 2.5% of farmland but a much larger share of the world's insecticides.
Most garment workers, mostly women, earn less than a living wage.
stages: Washing & drying|2|A quarter or more of lifetime carbon
End of life|2|Under 1% becomes new clothing
deps: Rivers in dry places|Cotton irrigation shrank the Aral Sea to a tenth of its size.
Garment workers|About 60 million people, mostly women.
Cheap energy|Textile mills run largely on coal and gas.
alts: Buy it second-hand|Almost all of the footprint is in making it. Second-hand skips that.|-0.5,-0.5,0,0,0.5|EASY|20|8000
Wear it twice as long|Doubling a garment's life roughly halves its yearly footprint.|-2,-2.5,-0.5,-1.5,-1.5|EASY|10|4000
Wash cold, line dry|Cuts the use-phase energy by more than half.|-2.5,-3.5,-0.5,-2.5,-2.5|EASY|50|0
qa: Is polyester better than cotton?|It uses far less water and land, but it is made from oil, sheds microplastic fibres in every wash and never biodegrades. Neither is clean; wearing whatever you own for longer beats both.
Is organic cotton worth it?|It avoids synthetic pesticides and is usually rain-fed, which is better for farmers and rivers. Yields are lower, so it needs somewhat more land.
src: Ellen MacArthur Foundation, A New Textiles Economy

name: Jeans
unit: one pair of jeans, from cotton field to end of life
headline: One pair of jeans uses about 3,800 litres of water and emits as much carbon as driving 110 km, according to Levi's own life-cycle study.
why: About 33 kg CO₂e over its life; fabric production and home washing are the biggest parts.
About 3,800 litres: two-thirds to grow the cotton, most of the rest in home washing.
Sandblasting denim to look worn caused fatal lung disease in workers before many brands banned it.
Indigo dye and finishing chemicals turn rivers blue near denim towns.
Made in the same low-wage supply chains as other clothing.
stages: Washing at home|2|23% of the water
deps: Cotton-growing rivers|Indus, Yellow River, Colorado: all over-drawn.
Denim-town waterways|Xintang in China and Tehuacán in Mexico are well-known pollution hotspots.
alts: Wash every ten wears, not every two|Levi's found this cuts lifetime water and climate impact by up to 80% of the care phase.|-3,-3,-0.5,-2.5,-2.5|EASY|8|700
Second-hand or vintage|Denim lasts decades: one of the best things to buy used.|-0.5,-0.5,0,0,0.5|EASY|30|3500
Repair instead of replace|A patch or a new zip adds years.|-2,-2,-0.5,-1.5,-1|MEDIUM|15|1800
qa: Do jeans really not need washing?|Rarely. Denim hides dirt and airs out well. Spot clean, air them, and wash cold when they actually need it.
src: Levi Strauss & Co., Life Cycle of a Jean 2015

name: Trainers
unit: one pair of synthetic trainers
headline: A typical pair of trainers has 65 separate parts and takes 360 steps to make. That is why almost none are ever recycled.
why: About 14 kg CO₂e a pair, two-thirds from manufacturing in coal-powered factories.
Leather tanning and synthetic materials both pollute water.
Good shoes keep people walking and running.
Glued-together plastics and rubber last centuries in landfill.
Footwear assembly is labour-intensive and concentrated where wages are lowest.
stages: End of life|2|About 22 billion pairs are made a year; most end in landfill
deps: Petrochemicals|Foam soles, uppers and glue are mostly oil-based.
Factory labour in Asia|Vietnam, China and Indonesia make most of the world's trainers.
alts: Resole or repair|A cobbler can double a shoe's life.|-2,-1.5,2,-1,-1|MEDIUM|7|0
Buy fewer, wear them out|The average person buys several pairs a year and wears a few.|-2,-2,2,-1.5,-2|EASY|14|0
Brands with take-back or resale|Keeps pairs in use longer.|-2,-2,2,-1,-2|EASY|5|0
qa: Are 'recycled' or 'vegan' trainers better?|Recycled content lowers the material footprint a little. 'Vegan leather' is usually plastic. How long you wear them matters more than what the label says.

name: Bag
unit: one leather or synthetic bag over its life
headline: A cotton tote must be used about 130 times to beat a single plastic bag on climate. A bag only becomes green by being used.
why: Leather carries part of a cow's footprint; synthetics are made from oil.
Tanning is water-intensive and chromium from tanneries poisons rivers.
Harmless to carry. Tannery workers have high rates of skin and lung disease.
Cattle ranching for meat and leather drives deforestation.
Tannery clusters in South Asia are among the most polluted workplaces on Earth.
stages: Years of use|0|The longer the better
deps: The beef industry|Leather is a co-product that makes ranching more profitable.
Tannery towns|Kanpur, Hazaribagh and others bear the pollution.
alts: Use the one you own for a decade|Good bags last. Impact per year falls with every year.|-1.5,-1.5,0,-1,-1|EASY|10|0
Second-hand|A mature resale market exists for bags.|-0.5,-0.5,0,0,0.5|EASY|30|0
Vegetable-tanned or recycled materials|Avoids chromium.|-2.5,-2,0,-2,-1|MEDIUM|0|0
qa: Is leather a by-product, so impact-free?|It is a co-product, not waste. Hides are worth money to the meat industry, so buying leather supports ranching, though less than buying beef does.
src: UK Environment Agency, Life Cycle Assessment of Carrier Bags 2011

name: Gold & jewellery
unit: one gold ring
headline: Mining the gold for a single ring leaves behind about 20 tonnes of waste rock.
why: Newly mined gold emits tens of tonnes of CO₂e per kilo.
Cyanide and mercury from gold processing contaminate rivers for generations.
Small-scale gold mining is the world's largest source of mercury pollution, which damages the nervous system.
Gold mining is a leading cause of deforestation in the Amazon and pollutes whole river systems.
Linked to conflict financing, child labour and dangerous work in small-scale mines; also a livelihood for millions.
deps: Rainforest rivers|Illegal mining has scarred large parts of the Amazon.
About 15 million small-scale miners|Many work without protection.
alts: Recycled or heirloom gold|Gold can be melted and reused endlessly, with a fraction of the footprint.|-1,-0.5,0,-0.5,0|EASY|100|0
Fairmined or Fairtrade certified gold|Traceable, with mercury controls and fair pay.|-3.5,-3,-1,-3,0.5|MEDIUM|0|0
Lab-grown stones|No mine at all.|-2,-1,0,-0.5,0|EASY|0|0
qa: Why does so little metal cause so much waste?|Ore grades are tiny: a tonne of rock may hold only a gram or two of gold. Everything else is crushed, treated with chemicals and left behind.

name: Smartphone
unit: one smartphone over a three-year life
headline: About 80% of this phone's carbon footprint was emitted before you ever switched it on. Keeping it one more year is greener than any feature of a new one.
why: Around 60–80 kg CO₂e, mostly from making the chips and screen.
About 12,000 litres to manufacture, mainly for mining and ultra-pure water in chip factories.
Screens affect sleep and attention; miners and recyclers face toxic exposure.
Contains some 60 elements, mined on every continent.
Most of the world's cobalt comes from the DR Congo, where child labour in small mines is documented. The phone also connects billions of people to information, money and each other.
stages: Chips & display|3|Extreme energy and water use
Charging|1|Only about 1 kg CO₂e a year
End of life|2|Only about a fifth of e-waste is properly recycled
deps: Cobalt from the DR Congo|About 70% of world supply.
Chip factories in Taiwan and Korea|Among the most water- and energy-hungry plants on Earth.
Rare earth mines|Essential for speakers, vibration and screen colours.
alts: Keep it a fourth and fifth year|A new battery costs little and saves most of a new phone's footprint.|-2.5,-3,-1,-2,-2.5|EASY|20|4000
Buy refurbished|About 80–90% lower footprint than new.|-1.5,-1.5,-1,-1,-0.5|EASY|50|10000
Hand the old one on|Sell, donate or recycle it: a drawer is the worst place for it.|-3,-3.5,-1,-2.5,-3|EASY|10|0
qa: Does charging my phone matter?|Barely. A year of charging is about 1 kg CO₂e, roughly 1% of the phone's footprint. How long you keep the phone matters about a hundred times more.
What happens to old phones?|The world generated 62 million tonnes of e-waste in 2022 and formally recycled under a quarter of it. A tonne of phones contains far more gold than a tonne of gold ore.
Why cobalt?|It stabilises lithium-ion batteries. Battery makers are shifting to low-cobalt and cobalt-free chemistries, partly because of the human-rights record.
src: Apple and Fairphone product environmental reports
Amnesty International, This Is What We Die For
Friends of the Earth, Mind Your Step

name: Laptop
unit: one laptop over a four-year life
headline: Making this laptop emitted about as much carbon as running it for the next fifteen years.
why: About 200–350 kg CO₂e, 75–85% of it from manufacturing.
Chip and screen fabrication need huge volumes of ultra-pure water.
Long sitting and screen time; toxic exposure for informal e-waste recyclers.
Dozens of mined metals and a growing e-waste stream.
Mineral supply chains carry labour risks. A laptop is also a tool for education, work and creativity.
stages: Electricity in use|1|About 20–50 kWh a year
deps: Semiconductor fabs|One advanced fab can use as much water as a small city.
Critical minerals|Cobalt, lithium, tin, tantalum, gold.
alts: Use it for six to eight years|Upgrade memory and battery instead of replacing.|-3,-3,-0.5,-2,-1.5|EASY|40|0
Buy refurbished|Business-grade laptops are built to last and cheap used.|-2,-2,-0.5,-1,-0.5|EASY|200|0
Choose a repairable model|Look for replaceable battery, memory and storage.|-3.5,-3.5,-0.5,-2.5,-2|MEDIUM|20|0
qa: Is the cloud part of my laptop's footprint?|Yes, indirectly. Streaming and AI run in data centres that use about 1.5% of the world's electricity, a share that is rising.
src: Dell and Apple product carbon footprints

name: Television & screens
unit: one large TV over an eight-year life
headline: A 55-inch TV's footprint is split roughly half and half between making it and watching it, so screen size is a climate choice.
why: Around 400–1,000 kg CO₂e over its life.
Panel manufacturing is water-intensive.
Long sedentary hours are linked to worse health.
Mining, plus potent fluorinated gases used in panel making.
Shared entertainment and news; electronics supply-chain labour risks.
stages: Electricity in use|3|100–200 kWh a year
deps: The power grid|Its footprint in use depends on how your electricity is made.
Panel factories|Use nitrogen trifluoride, a gas 17,000 times more warming than CO₂.
alts: Keep the one you have|A working TV always beats a new efficient one on carbon.|-3.5,-2.5,-1.5,-1.5,-1|EASY|50|0
Go a size smaller, lower the brightness|Energy use rises steeply with screen area.|-4,-3,-1.5,-2,-1.5|EASY|30|0
qa: Should I unplug it?|Modern standby uses under a watt, so it matters little. Brightness settings and screen size matter much more.

name: Headphones
unit: one small electronic device over its life
headline: Wireless earbuds often die when their glued-in batteries do, after two or three years. They are among the least repairable things we own.
why: Roughly 5–25 kg CO₂e, mostly manufacturing.
Mining and electronics manufacturing.
Loud listening is putting over a billion young people at risk of hearing loss.
Small, mixed-material, hard to recycle.
The same mineral supply chains as phones.
stages: End of life|3|Rarely recycled; batteries can cause fires in waste trucks
deps: Lithium and cobalt|Even a tiny battery starts in a mine.
Rare earth magnets|Every speaker has one.
alts: Wired or repairable models|Replaceable batteries and cables mean a decade of use.|-1.5,-1.5,-1,-1,-1|EASY|3|0
Take old electronics to a collection point|Never the household bin.|-2,-2,-1,-1.5,-2|EASY|0|0
qa: Why can't small electronics be recycled easily?|They are glued, tiny and mix dozens of materials. Recovering a few milligrams of metal costs more than it is worth, unless the product was designed to come apart.

name: Furniture
unit: one piece of furniture over its life
headline: A solid wood chair stores carbon for as long as it exists. Europeans alone throw away about 10 million tonnes of furniture every year.
why: About 10–100 kg CO₂e depending on size; foam, metal and particleboard cost the most.
Timber, cotton and foam production.
Good furniture supports posture and rest; new particleboard and foam can give off fumes.
Up to a third of traded tropical timber is thought to be illegally logged. Certified wood can support well-managed forest.
Carpentry is skilled local work; flat-pack supply chains are less transparent.
stages: End of life|2|Most is landfilled or burned
deps: Forests|Slow-grown hardwood takes 50–100 years to replace.
Oil|Foam, laminate and synthetic fabrics are petrochemicals.
alts: Buy second-hand solid wood|Often better made than new, with no new footprint.|-0.5,0,1,0,0.5|EASY|40|0
FSC-certified new wood|Traceable to responsibly managed forest.|-2,-1.5,1,0,0.5|EASY|0|0
Repair, reupholster, repaint|Extends life for a fraction of the material.|-1,-0.5,1,-0.5,1|MEDIUM|30|0
qa: Is wood always the green choice?|Wood from well-managed forest is one of the best materials we have. Wood from cleared old-growth forest is one of the worst. The certificate is what tells them apart.
src: European Environmental Bureau, Circular Economy in the Furniture Sector
INTERPOL / UNEP, Green Carbon, Black Trade

name: Book & paper
unit: one paperback book
headline: A paperback emits about as much carbon as a cup of coffee with milk each day for a week, and can be read by a dozen people over fifty years.
why: About 1–3 kg CO₂e to make and ship.
Paper mills are heavy water users, though most of the water is returned.
Reading is linked to lower stress and slower cognitive decline.
Depends on the forest: recycled and certified paper is low impact; plantations that replace natural forest are not.
Literacy and access to books are among the strongest drivers of opportunity.
deps: Working forests|Paper demand can either protect or replace them.
Libraries and second-hand shops|They multiply every book's value.
alts: Library or second-hand|The same story, shared footprint.|-0.5,-0.5,2,0,5|EASY|10|0
Pass it on when you're done|A book on a shelf serves one reader.|-1.5,-1.5,2,-1,5|EASY|5|0
qa: Paper book or e-reader?|An e-reader costs about as much carbon as 30–60 paper books. If you read more than that on it before replacing it, the e-reader wins.

name: Lamp & lighting
unit: one LED bulb, used three hours a day for a year
headline: An LED uses about a sixth of the electricity of the old bulbs it replaced. The switch to LEDs is one of the fastest efficiency wins in history.
why: About 10 kWh a year: roughly 5 kg CO₂e on an average grid.
Power stations use water for cooling.
Good light supports safety, study and mood; bright blue-rich light late at night disrupts sleep.
Light at night disorients insects, birds and turtles.
Light after dark extends the day for work and learning. About 700 million people still live without electricity.
deps: The grid|The same lamp is nearly carbon-free on renewable power.
Darkness|Many species need real night.
alts: Switch it off when you leave|Still the cheapest kilowatt-hour.|-1.5,-0.5,2,0,3|EASY|3|0
Warm, shielded light outdoors|Point it down and use a sensor: better for wildlife and for seeing stars.|-1.5,-1,2,0.5,3|EASY|2|0
Renewable electricity tariff|Changes the footprint of everything you plug in.|-0.5,-0.5,2,-0.5,3|MEDIUM|400|0
qa: Are LEDs bad for wildlife?|Their efficiency made light so cheap that we now use much more of it. The night sky is getting brighter by nearly 10% a year in places, which harms insects and migrating birds.

name: Mug & tableware
unit: one reusable mug or dish over years of use
headline: After about 40 uses this mug has a smaller footprint than the paper cups it replaced. After a thousand, it is practically free.
why: About 1 kg CO₂e to fire in a kiln; then only the washing-up.
Washing uses a little water each time.
Inert, safe and plastic-free.
Clay and sand are abundant; no waste while it lasts.
Shared tables and meals are where community happens.
stages: End of life|1|Not recyclable, but lasts decades
deps: Hot water|Most of its lifetime footprint is how you wash it.
alts: Keep using it|Reusables only win if they are actually reused.|-0.5,-0.5,0.5,0,0.5|EASY|5|0
Run the dishwasher full, on eco|Uses less water and energy than washing by hand under a running tap.|-0.5,-0.5,0.5,-0.5,0.5|EASY|40|5000
qa: Is reusable always better than disposable?|Only after enough uses. A ceramic mug needs tens of uses to beat paper cups, a steel bottle a few dozen to beat plastic ones. A reusable you use five times is worse than the disposables.
src: UNEP, Single-use beverage cups and their alternatives 2021
CIRAIG life-cycle study of coffee cups

name: Plastic bag & packaging
unit: one single-use plastic bag or wrapper
headline: This will be used for about twelve minutes and last for centuries. Only about 9% of all plastic ever made has been recycled.
why: Tiny per item: about 10–30 g CO₂e. The problem is the number and the afterlife.
Little water to make; lasting pollution of rivers and seas.
Breaks into microplastics now found in food, water, air and human blood.
Over a thousand marine species are known to eat or get tangled in plastic.
Much rich-country plastic waste is exported to poorer countries, where waste pickers handle it without protection.
deps: Fossil fuels|Plastics are the oil industry's main growth market.
Waste pickers|About 20 million people worldwide do most of the world's plastic recycling by hand.
alts: Carry a bag you already own|Any bag, used many times.|0,0,0,0,0|EASY|2|0
Choose loose or refill|Skip the packaging rather than recycle it.|0,0,0,0,0|MEDIUM|10|0
Sort it properly|Clean, sorted plastic is the only kind that gets recycled.|-0.5,-0.5,-1,-2,-1|EASY|3|0
qa: Is paper or cotton better?|Not automatically. A paper bag needs about 3 uses and a cotton tote about 130 to beat one plastic bag on climate. Reuse is what matters, whatever the material.
Where does plastic go when I recycle it?|It depends on the type and your local system. Bottles and rigid containers have real markets. Films and mixed plastics mostly do not.

name: Toy
unit: one plastic or plush toy over its life
headline: About 90% of toys are made of plastic and most are played with for only a few months. The best toy is usually someone else's old one.
why: A few kilos of CO₂e each, mostly plastic and shipping.
Plastic and textile production.
Play builds brains, bodies and friendships.
Mixed plastics and electronics are nearly impossible to recycle.
Play is a child's right. Toy factories have a long record of excessive overtime.
deps: Petrochemicals|Almost every toy starts as oil.
Factory workers|Most toys are made in a few provinces of China.
alts: Second-hand, swap or toy library|Children rarely care whether it is new.|-0.5,0,2,0,2.5|EASY|10|0
Fewer, sturdier, open-ended toys|Blocks outlast a hundred gadgets.|-1,-1,2.5,-1,2|EASY|10|0
Hand it on|Every toy has several childhoods in it.|-1,-1,2,-1,2.5|EASY|5|0
qa: Are wooden toys better?|Usually: they last longer, can be repaired and are simpler to dispose of. But a plastic toy that is used for ten years by five children beats a wooden one used once.

name: Cigarettes & vapes
unit: one pack of 20 cigarettes
headline: Cigarette butts are the most littered object on Earth: about 4.5 trillion a year, each one a plastic filter soaked in toxins.
why: Tobacco growing and curing emit about 84 million tonnes of CO₂ a year.
About 3.7 litres of water per cigarette.
Tobacco kills more than 8 million people a year, including over a million non-smokers.
Curing tobacco burns forests; butts leach nicotine and heavy metals into water.
Child labour is common on tobacco farms; smoking deepens poverty and costs health systems heavily.
deps: Farmland in poor countries|Land that could grow food.
Addiction|The business model depends on it.
alts: Quit, with support|Stop-smoking services and nicotine replacement roughly triple the chance of success.|0,0,4,0,2|BIG|6|27000
Never drop a butt|If you smoke, carry a pocket ashtray.|-2,-2,-5,-2,-4|EASY|0|0
qa: Are vapes better?|For the smoker's health, probably less harmful than smoking, though not harmless. For the environment, disposable vapes add lithium batteries and plastic to the litter stream, with millions thrown away every week.

name: Home appliance
unit: one large appliance, running for a year
headline: Your fridge never sleeps. The gases inside old fridges and air conditioners can warm the planet thousands of times more than CO₂ if they leak.
why: Roughly 50–250 kg CO₂e a year in electricity, plus manufacture and refrigerant leaks.
Washing machines and dishwashers use thousands of litres a year; power stations use more.
Refrigeration prevents food poisoning; washing machines and cooling protect health.
Mined metals, and refrigerants that harm the climate if released.
The washing machine freed billions of hours, mostly women's. Over 700 million people still lack a fridge.
stages: End of life|2|Must be degassed properly
deps: The power grid|Its footprint follows your electricity mix.
Refrigerant recovery|Proper disposal is listed among the most effective climate solutions.
alts: Repair before replacing|Most failures are a cheap part.|-3.5,-2,3,-1,3|MEDIUM|30|0
Use it smartly|Full loads, 30 °C washes, fridge at 4 °C, clean door seals.|-3.5,-2,3,-1.5,3|EASY|60|5000
When it truly dies, buy the top efficiency class|And make sure the old one is collected and degassed.|-3,-2,3,-1,3|MEDIUM|80|3000
qa: Should I replace an old appliance to save energy?|Only if it is very old or broken. For most appliances under about ten years old, the footprint of making a new one outweighs the saving.
src: Hans Rosling, The Magic Washing Machine

name: Tap, shower & toilet
unit: one person's showers and tap use for a year
headline: An eight-minute shower uses about 70 litres of drinking-quality water, and heating it is usually a household's second-biggest energy use.
why: Heating water emits several hundred kilos of CO₂e a person each year.
A typical person in a rich country uses around 140 litres at home every day.
Clean water and sanitation are the greatest public-health advance in history.
Water taken from rivers and aquifers leaves less for wetlands and fish; wastewater carries nutrients and medicines back.
2.2 billion people still lack safely managed drinking water.
deps: A river or aquifer you have probably never seen|Every tap has a watershed.
Water workers and pipes|Invisible until they fail.
alts: Five-minute showers|The most effective home water saving.|-3.5,-4,4.5,-1,4|EASY|100|10000
Low-flow shower head|Same feel, half the water and heat.|-3.5,-4,4.5,-1,4|EASY|150|15000
Fix drips|A dripping tap can waste 5,000 litres a year.|-4,-4,4.5,-1.5,4|EASY|5|5000
qa: Bath or shower?|A short shower wins. A full bath is about 150 litres; a five-minute shower with an efficient head is about 40.
Where does my water come from?|Find out: knowing your river or aquifer changes how you see the tap. Most water utilities publish their sources.

name: Cosmetics & toiletries
unit: one bottle or tube of a personal-care product
headline: Palm oil derivatives are in roughly 70% of cosmetics, under more than 200 different ingredient names.
why: About 1–3 kg CO₂e a bottle; for shampoo and shower gel, most of it is the hot water you use with it.
Rinse-off products go straight down the drain.
Hygiene is good for health; some ingredients are irritants or under review.
Palm oil drives deforestation; UV filters and microplastics reach rivers and reefs.
Mica for shimmer is linked to child labour in India; palm plantations to land conflicts.
deps: Tropical plantations|Indonesia and Malaysia grow about 85% of palm oil.
Wastewater treatment|Not everything is filtered out.
alts: Solid bars and refills|No bottle, less water shipped.|-1,-1.5,0.5,-1.5,-1|EASY|3|0
Use less, finish it|Most of us use twice the dose we need.|-1,-1.5,0.5,-2,-1|EASY|3|0
Certified palm oil and traceable mica|RSPO and Responsible Mica Initiative members.|-1.5,-2,0.5,-1.5,-0.5|MEDIUM|0|0
qa: Should I boycott palm oil?|Most experts say no. Oil palm yields four to ten times more oil per hectare than alternatives, so replacing it would need more land. Certified, deforestation-free palm oil is the better ask.
src: Terre des Hommes, Beauty and a Beast

name: Sports gear
unit: one piece of sports equipment over its life
headline: The lowest-carbon gym is the one you already own: a ball, a rope, a pair of shoes and somewhere to move.
why: A few kilos of CO₂e for simple gear; much more for carbon fibre or electronics.
Rubber, plastics and textiles.
Regular activity cuts the risk of early death by up to 30%.
Synthetic materials; artificial pitches shed microplastic infill.
Sport builds teams, confidence and belonging.
deps: Somewhere to play|Parks and pitches are public health infrastructure.
alts: Borrow, rent or buy used|Especially for sports you are just trying.|-0.5,-0.5,4.5,0,3.5|EASY|10|0
Use it|The only bad sports gear is the kind that stays in the cupboard.|-2,-1.5,5,-1,4|EASY|0|0
qa: Do the benefits outweigh the footprint?|For simple gear that is used regularly, clearly yes. Health and social gains from regular movement are among the largest of any consumer product.

name: Money
unit: your savings and pension over a year, in a typical large bank
headline: The world's 60 biggest banks have put about 6.9 trillion dollars into fossil fuels since the Paris Agreement. Some of that is your money, working while you sleep.
why: Banks and pension funds lend and invest deposits; a typical portfolio still funds oil, gas and coal expansion.
Financed mining, energy and agriculture all use water.
Indirect.
Finance flows to deforestation-linked commodities are far larger than flows to conservation.
Finance builds homes and businesses too. What it does depends on where it is directed.
stages: Bank lending & investment|3|Where the impact is decided
deps: Your attention|Most people never ask what their bank funds.
Regulation and disclosure|Banks now publish financed emissions; few customers read them.
alts: Move to a bank with a fossil-free policy|An hour of admin, then it works for you every day.|1,0,0,0.5,1|MEDIUM|0|0
Check your pension's default fund|For many people, their largest financial asset and biggest lever.|1.5,0,0,1,1|MEDIUM|0|0
Ask your bank the question|Customer pressure is one of the few things banks track closely.|-3,-2,0,-2.5,0.5|EASY|0|0
qa: Is this really bigger than my lifestyle footprint?|It can be, but estimates vary a lot and depend on how much you hold and where. Treat it as a large lever of uncertain size rather than a precise number.
How do I check my bank?|Search for its name with 'fossil fuel financing'. Independent trackers rank banks every year.

name: Petrol car
unit: one petrol car, driven a typical 12,000 km in a year
headline: This car is parked about 95% of the time. When it moves, a tonne and a half of metal usually carries one person.
why: About 2–4.6 tonnes of CO₂ a year from the exhaust, plus 6–10 tonnes to build it.
Fuel refining and manufacturing; road run-off carries oil and tyre dust into rivers.
Air pollution, inactivity and crashes: road traffic kills about 1.2 million people a year.
Roads fragment habitat; tyre wear is one of the largest sources of microplastics in the ocean.
Freedom and access for those who have one; danger, noise and lost space for those who do not.
deps: Oil|About a quarter of world oil goes to passenger cars.
Public space|A parked car takes about 12 m², often of public land, usually for free.

name: Bicycle
unit: one bicycle, ridden regularly for a year in place of some car trips
headline: Cycling is the most energy-efficient way any animal or machine has ever travelled. People who cycle to work have about 40% lower risk of early death.
why: Making it costs about 100–200 kg CO₂e once. Each kilometre ridden instead of driven saves about 150–250 g, so regular riders are deep in credit. Scored as a replacement for some car trips.
Steel, aluminium and rubber production.
Among the best things a person can do for heart, mind and lifespan.
No exhaust, almost no noise, a tenth of a car's road space.
Affordable mobility for almost everyone, and it makes streets safer and friendlier.

qa: Is an e-bike still green?|Yes. Its battery and electricity add only a few grams of CO₂ per kilometre, and e-bikes replace more car trips than ordinary bikes do.
